1 · Modeling · Sec. III

From joint motion to tip motion

The controller requires a differential model from joint motion to tip motion that can be evaluated at the control rate. Its analytic part follows from the arm kinematics and the tendon anchors, and its soft part, which maps span changes to the motion of the tip relative to the EE, is identified from probing motions. The workspace shows the simulated UR10 of the paper, whose soft extension is a Cosserat rod loaded by two elastic tendons.

Span kinematics (Sec. III-C)

Tendon i runs from its anchor a_i(\q) on a link upstream of the EE to its entry point b_i(\q), which is fixed in \{B\} at \Bb_i. The exterior span is the straight length of the tendon between the two points:

b_i(\q)=p_B(\q)+R_B(\q)\,\Bb_i,\qquad \lo_i(\q)=\|a_i(\q)-b_i(\q)\|

With d_i the unit vector from b_i to a_i, the span rates are \dot{\blo}=\Jlq\qd (3), and row i of the span Jacobian is

[\Jlq]_i=d_i^{\T}\big(J_{a_i}^v-J_B^v+[R_B\,\Bb_i]_\times J_B^\omega\big).

This matrix depends only on the arm kinematics and on the anchors and entry points, not on the mechanics of the soft extension.

Soft response (Sec. III-D)

A taut tendon runs along its exterior span and then along an interior path inside the soft extension. Its tension depends on the total stretch, so the linearized tension-stretch relation includes the length changes of both parts, with \zv the shape coordinates and K_a the stiffnesses of the taut, unsaturated tendons:

\dot{\tauv}=K_a\big(\dot{\blo}+\Jlz\dot{\zv}\big)

With the shape response \Jzt=\partial\zv/\partial\tauv, the span-to-tension map and the span-to-deformation map are

C_\tau=\big(I-K_a\Jlz\Jzt\big)^{-1}K_a
\VDB=\Jspan\dot{\blo},\qquad \Jspan:=\JDt C_\tau.

The controller depends on the soft mechanics only through \Jspan.

Tip velocity (Sec. III-E)

The twist of the distal frame \{D\} is the sum of the transport, the motion that the EE imposes on the soft extension at fixed shape, and the deformation produced by the tendons:

\Jtr=\begin{bmatrix}J_B^v-[p_D-p_B]_\times J_B^\omega\\ J_B^\omega\end{bmatrix}
J_D=\Jtr+\Rbar\,\Jspan\Jlq,\qquad J_t=SJ_D.

Identified model (Sec. III-F)

Probing motions move the arm through configurations whose spans cover a grid around the spans at \q_0, while a camera measures the tip and a few body points p_j. A map fitted to these samples gives \Jspanh, which an online secant (Broyden) correction adapts:

\JDh=\Jtr+\Rbar\,\Jspanh\Jlq
J_{p_j}=J_B^v-[R_B\,{}^{B}p_j]_\times J_B^\omega+R_B\frac{\partial\,{}^{B}p_j}{\partial\blo}\Jlq

The identification is local, so the model is used only in the identified span domain \Lspan=[\bm\ell^-,\bm\ell^+], covered by the probes.

Try this

  1. Move joints 1–3 with the sliders. The arm carries the anchors and the EE together, so the spans do not change and the soft extension is only transported (columns 1–3 of \Jlq are zero).
  2. Move joints 4–6. The wrist moves the entry points relative to the anchors on the forearm and the wrist: the spans and tensions change, and the soft extension bends. Joint 4 turns about an axis through anchor 1, so it changes only span 2.
  3. Press Fix shape here, then move a joint: the faded tube is the soft extension transported at fixed shape, and the gap between its tip and the tip is the deformation term of (9).
  4. Switch to Null-space motion with the position-constrained EE and hold a direction: p_B stays where it is while the tip moves through the reorientation of the EE and the bending of the soft extension. Under the fulcrum, the tool axis keeps passing through c. The last direction leaves the tip in place, while the spans and tensions change.
  5. In Identified model, probe and fit with a range of ±10 mm, then ±22 mm, and compare the validation errors (1.5 and 5.5 mm in the paper).

The arm and the tendon geometry give \Jlq and the transport exactly; only the local map from span changes to deformation, \Jspan, has to be identified, and only inside the span domain that the probes covered.
